_readme: Hand-researched map annotations — the facts no table in quarm.db carries.
COORDINATES are game coordinates, the same convention as spawn2.x/y/z.
Note that EQ's /loc prints them in the order y, x, z — so a /loc reading of
The in-app annotation editor captures coordinates from a map click, so this
only matters when hand-editing.
CATEGORY is one of: wall, hazard, note. Kept deliberately small — a category
earns its own map layer, and a layer nobody toggles is worse than a clear
label. Put the specifics in the label: 'Fake wall — ...', 'One-way wall — ...'.
EVIDENCE is required and is the point of this file. These facts are safe to
record because a fact about the game is not anyone's creative work — 'there
is a fake wall here' is an observation, published across Brewall, PQDI and
several map packs. What is not safe is lifting one map set's annotation file
wholesale as a dataset. So every row states where the fact was confirmed, and
the standard is: verified in game, or corroborated by two independent public
sources. A row without real evidence should not be here; mapgen rejects an
empty evidence string rather than letting one through quietly.
This file is intentionally near-empty. The pipeline is built; the corpus is
human research and cannot be invented from memory without producing
confident-looking coordinates that send people into walls that are not there.
